content.text: {"title":"Four Characters and a Progress Bar: What tqdm Promises While It Prints","premise":"A caller has a four-item list and a loop that does real work, and wants to see progress without writing any printing logic. The list is handed to `tqdm(...)`: from that moment it is no longer just a list but the payload of a progress meter that must allocate a global write lock, start a background thread, probe the terminal, render a frame, throttle itself, and clean up after the loop ends — all on `sys.stderr`, all without changing what the loop iterates over. This story follows that list through one real run and asks, at each step, what is guaranteed and what could go wrong.","chapters":[{"n":1,"title":"Before the list is even looked at: a lock, a registry, a thread","trace_lines":[2,21],"data_in":"`tqdm(['a','b','c','d'])` is called; Python routes to `tqdm.__new__(cls=<type>)`, which ignores the list entirely","data_out":"`<tqdm.std.tqdm object at 0x109742cf0>` — a bare instance, already registered in `tqdm._instances`, with a process-wide `TqdmDefaultWriteLock` built and a daemon `TMonitor` thread running","code":["tqdm/std.py:664-678","tqdm/std.py:766-771","tqdm/std.py:74-126","tqdm/_monitor.py:16-60"],"inputs":["iterable=['a','b','c','d']"],"characters":["tqdm.__new__","tqdm.get_lock","TqdmDefaultWriteLock","TqdmDefaultWriteLock.create_mp_lock","tqdm._instances (WeakSet)","TMonitor","tqdm.monitor_interval"],"facts":["`__new__` runs before any user argument is validated: side effects (lock creation, instance registration, thread start) happen even for a bar that will later be disabled or rejected.","The write lock is created lazily on first use: `get_lock()` builds a `TqdmDefaultWriteLock` only if `cls._lock` is unset, so importing tqdm creates no multiprocessing objects.","`TqdmDefaultWriteLock` holds both a class-level threading `RLock` (created at import) and a lazily created `multiprocessing.RLock`; `acquire` takes them in order and `release` reverses the order.","The instance is added to the `WeakSet` `_instances` before `__init__` runs, which is why the `disable` and unknown-kwargs paths in `__init__` must explicitly `_instances.remove(self)`.","A monitor thread is started only if `monitor_interval` is truthy and no live monitor exists; it is a `daemon` thread named `tqdm_monitor` with an `atexit`-registered non-joining kill signal, so interpreter exit cannot deadlock on it.","If `TMonitor(...)` raises, the exception is swallowed: a `TqdmMonitorWarning` is emitted and `monitor_interval` is set to 0, permanently disabling monitoring for the process rather than failing the caller's bar."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q1.1","question":"A background thread now exists for the whole process — does the next bar start another one, and who stops it?"},{"id":"q1.2","question":"This instance is in the global registry before it is even configured; the caller can redirect it with `file=`.","`total` is inferred from `len(iterable)` inside a `try/except (TypeError, AttributeError)`; a generator simply yields `total=None` and a counter-only display instead of an error. `total == float('inf')` is normalised to `None`.","The stream is wrapped by `DisableOnWriteError`, which intercepts `write`/`flush` and, on `OSError` with `errno == 5` or a `ValueError` containing 'closed', sets `miniters = float('inf')` on a weak proxy to the bar instead of propagating — a broken terminal mutes the bar rather than crashing the loop.","Terminal size is probed via `os.get_terminal_size` inside a bare `except Exception`; here it returns `(None, None)`, meaning tqdm will fall back to a fixed-width bar with no truncation.","`ascii` is auto-detected from the stream's `encoding`; if encoding lookup fails, `_supports_unicode` returns `False` and the bar degrades to the ASCII charset.","`miniters=None` turns on `dynamic_miniters`, i.e. tqdm will tune its own display frequency; an explicit `position=n` is stored as `-n` to mark it fixed and exempt from later repositioning.","`status_printer` is only created when `gui=False`; GUI subclasses skip it and must override `display`/`close`, otherwise `display()` raises `TqdmDeprecationWarning`.","The printer keeps `last_len` in a one-element list and pads each new line with spaces to erase the previous, longer line — in-place updating depends entirely on the console honouring `\\r`, and breaks (newline per refresh) if a line exceeds the terminal width.","`status_printer` flushes both stdout and stderr once up-front when writing to either, to reduce interleaving with ordinary prints.","`start_t` is deliberately set last in `__init__`, after the first refresh, so the monitor thread (which skips instances lacking `start_t`) cannot observe a half-built bar."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q3.1","question":"Position 0 was free because this is the only bar — what happens to positions when bars come and go, e.g. nested loops?"}],"answers":[]},{"n":4,"title":"The first frame: rendering 0/4 and committing it to stderr","trace_lines":[68,112],"data_in":"`tqdm.refresh(self, nolock=False, lock_args=None)` on a bar with `n=0, total=4, elapsed=0, ncols=None`","data_out":"`'  0%|          | 0/4 [00:00<?, ?it/s]'` written as `'\\r' + s` to stderr (38 chars); with `lock_args` it uses a non-blocking acquire and returns `False` without printing rather than waiting — that is how parallel bars avoid contention at the cost of dropped frames.","`display` refuses to draw bars beyond the screen: `pos >= nrows` returns `False`, and the row at `nrows - 1` is replaced by `' ... (more hidden) ...'`. With `nrows=None` the fallback is 20 rows.","Rendering is pure formatting over a snapshot: `format_dict` collects `n`, `total`, `elapsed`, and `rate` (EMA of dn over EMA of dt, `None` if no dt yet), and `format_meter` is a `@staticmethod` that can be called with those values alone.","With no rate yet, `format_meter` prints `?it/s` and `?` for remaining instead of dividing by zero; `remaining` is computed only `if rate and total`, and an `OverflowError` on the ETA datetime falls back to `datetime.max`.","`bar_format` is probed with a `FormatReplace` sentinel first: if the user's format string never references `{bar}`, the expensive `Bar` is never constructed.","`ncols=None` means no trimming: the bar is a fixed 10 cells and the whole line is printed untrimmed. With a known `ncols`, `disp_trim` cuts it to width and re-appends an ANSI reset if colour codes were cut.","`Bar` clamps `frac` into [0,1] with a `TqdmWarning` and rejects unknown colours with a warning rather than an exception — a bad `colour=` degrades to no colour.","Line length is measured with `disp_len`, which strips ANSI codes and counts East-Asian wide characters as 2, so padding stays correct for non-Latin descriptions.","The actual `write` call goes through `DisableOnWriteError.inner`, so every frame is written inside the error-swallowing wrapper from Chapter 2."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q4.1","question":"One frame has been painted at 0/4; how often will the bar be repainted as the loop runs — is any intermediate progress guaranteed?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q2.1","answer":"With `ncols=None` tqdm does not resize or trim: it renders a 10-cell bar and prints the full line. Width-dependent truncation (`disp_trim`) only happens when `ncols` is known or given, and in-place updating relies on the line fitting the console — which is exactly the 'bar wraps onto many lines' failure mode in the README's FAQ."},{"id":"q2.2","answer":"No. Writes pass through `DisableOnWriteError.inner`, which converts `errno==5` and 'closed' stream errors into `miniters = float('inf')` on a weak proxy of the bar. The loop keeps running, the bar silently stops updating, and the caller sees no exception."}]},{"n":5,"title":"Four items, no repaint: the loop runs and the bar closes itself","trace_lines":[113,119],"data_in":"`tqdm.__iter__(self)` — the generator wrapping `['a','b','c','d']`","data_out":"`'a'`, then the remaining items (`… tqdm.__iter__ ×4 more`); self.close()` sit in a `finally`, so the bar is closed on `break`, on exception, and on normal exhaustion — the terminal is left in a sane state even when the loop aborts.","`close()` guards with `if getattr(self, 'disable', True): return` and then sets `disable = True`, making it idempotent; `report()` is simply `not was_killed.is_set()`, so at most one monitor thread exists per process and it survives bar churn.","The monitor's job is bounded and defensive: every `sleep_interval` (default 10 s) it takes the write lock, and for instances with `miniters > 1` whose last print is older than `maxinterval` it forces `miniters = 1` and `refresh(nolock=True)`. It re-checks the kill event inside the loop to keep shutdown fast, and warns (`TqdmSynchronisationWarning`) if the instance set changed during iteration.","`monitor_interval = 10` is a class attribute: setting `tqdm.tqdm.monitor_interval = 0` before the first bar disables monitoring application-wide — a documented escape hatch for environments where an extra daemon thread is unacceptable."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[{"id":"q1.1","answer":"No second thread: `__new__` reuses `cls.monitor` because `report()` is `True`. So the display can legitimately show `0/4` after two items.","`elapsed` in `format_dict` is live (`_time() - start_t`), so the time field advances (0.053 s, 0.108 s) even while the counter is frozen.","`rate` is `None` until `_ema_dt()` is non-zero, which is why these frames still show `?it/s` despite elapsed time passing.","`set_description_str` is the variant that does not append `': '`; both mutate shared display state with no locking of their own — the lock is taken inside `refresh`."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q8.1","question":"The displayed counter is two items behind reality — does it ever catch up, and by what rule?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q5.1","answer":"Not permanently: the forced refreshes here show how the display is driven by `self.n` rather than by the loop, and Chapter 12 shows `close()` repainting a final, correct frame when `leave=True`. It checks the cheap counter gate first (`n - last_print_n >= miniters`) to avoid calling `time()` on every iteration, then the time gate (`dt >= mininterval` and past `start_t + delay`).","Rate is an exponential moving average of increments over intervals (`_ema_dn()/_ema_dt()`), not a simple average — recent speed dominates, controlled by `smoothing`. `EMA.__call__` divides by `1 - beta**calls` to de-bias early samples.","With `dynamic_miniters`, tqdm rewrites its own `miniters` after each print: normally `EMA(dn * mininterval/dt)`, but if `dt >= maxinterval` it resets to `dn * mininterval/dt` directly — this is the documented 'fast then slow iterations' hazard the monitor thread exists to rescue.","`miniters` can become a float (1.8125 here); the counter gate is a `>=` comparison, so fractional thresholds are fine.","`update` returns `True` only when a display was triggered, which is the documented hook for custom callbacks that want to piggyback on tqdm's throttling.","A negative `n` is tolerated (`last_print_n += n`) so meters that go backwards still auto-refresh correctly; `update` is a no-op when `disable` is set."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[{"id":"q4.1","answer":"Only when both gates open. The display is repainted when the counter has advanced at least `miniters` *and* at least `mininterval` seconds have elapsed since the last print (and `delay` has passed). tqdm guarantees it will not spam the terminal; it does not guarantee any particular number of intermediate frames — a short, fast loop may show only its first and last."},{"id":"q8.1","answer":"Here: `update(2)` publishes the two consumed items at once, and the frame jumps straight from `0/4` to `50%|█████ | 2/4`. After this print it is retuned again to ≈1.75 — a feedback loop that keeps print frequency near `mininterval` without calling the clock every iteration."}]},{"n":12,"title":"Closing down: leaving the registry, the truth about the rate, and a newline","trace_lines":[530,602],"data_in":"the generator's `finally` calls `tqdm.close(self)` on a bar with `n=4`, `pos=0`, `leave=True`","data_out":"instance removed from `_instances`; a probe write of `''`; final frame `'Processing d: 100%|██████████| 4/4 [00:00<00:00, 17.39it/s]'` at `pos=0` followed by `'\\n'`; `disable=True`","code":["tqdm/std.py:1270-1314","tqdm/std.py:687-715","tqdm/std.py:1316-1330","tqdm/utils.py:100-118"],"inputs":["leave=True"],"characters":["tqdm.close","tqdm._decr_instances","Comparable.__eq__","tqdm._comparable","tqdm.display","tqdm.clear","print_status"],"facts":["`close()` sets `disable = True` first, making multiple closes (loop `finally`, `__exit__`, `__del__`) safe and cheap.","`_decr_instances` removes the bar under the global lock, tolerating a missing entry (`KeyError` → pass), then repositions one overflowed unfixed bar (smallest `pos >= nrows - 1`) into the freed slot: on-screen order is not preserved, but blank lines and flicker are minimised.","Instance identity in the `WeakSet` uses `__hash__ = id(self)` while `Comparable.__eq__` compares `abs(pos)` — equality is by screen position, hashing by identity; the trace shows both being consulted during removal.","Before printing anything, `close` probes the stream with `fp_write('')` and returns quietly if it raises `ValueError` containing 'closed' — closing a bar after its output stream has gone is not an error.","`close` returns early (printing nothing) if the bar never displayed: no `last_print_t`, or `last_print_t < start_t + delay`.
